_source: Ma'am's impact list (screenshots, 2026-09-22). Every row below traces to a row in that list via `source`. Wording is restructured, NOT invented; where a row was ambiguous or unanswered it is marked OPEN or AMBIGUOUS rather than resolved.

principle.text: RM, HR, Admin or a similar privileged role can always see and search a hidden profile. Everyone else is governed by the rule on each screen below.

rules.name: Listed and marked
rules.text: The person appears for anyone who can open the screen, carrying the hidden-profile treatment (tinted row + icon).

rules.name: Privileged viewers only
rules.text: The row exists only for the named roles. For everyone else it is absent — not greyed out, not disabled. Absent.

rules.name: Not listed for anyone
rules.text: Excluded from the list, dropdown or result set for every viewer, privileged roles included.

rules.name: Reporting manager only
rules.text: Visible to the reporting manager alone — narrower than V2, which also includes HR and Admin.

rules.name: Not decided
rules.text: Ma'am's list raises this as a question. No rule has been chosen; a developer must not pick one.

portals.name: Global
portals.note: Applies across every portal, not to one screen.

rows.not: Every other role — the person returns no result
rows.flag: Ma'am wrote "restricted people wont be able to search". That reads two ways: (a) the person does not APPEAR in others' search results, or (b) the person cannot USE search. Row 1 of the same table says RM/HR/Admin can "see and search the person", so this is written as (a). If (b) was meant, that is an access change, not a visibility one, and belongs with Account Status instead.

portals.name: People
portals.note: The portal where HR must still be able to find the person. Reconciliation lives here.

rows.sees: Everyone with access to the People employee list
rows.treatment: Tinted row + incognito icon; hidden by default behind the Hidden filter

rows.flag: Ma'am bundled four screens into one row. They are four separate screens and are split here.
The only row where ma'am named the RM alone and explicitly wrote the negative side. HR and Admin are NOT listed here — confirm whether that is deliberate or whether the global principle overrides it.
rows.source: People > Will Come row 4 + Won't Come row 4

rows.sees: RM and higher admin / HR roles
rows.flag: Ma'am wrote "if possible". Removing a node from a hierarchy leaves a gap or an orphaned subtree — if the hidden person has reports, their reports' parent disappears. The chart's behaviour in that case is NOT DECIDED and is not a UI detail.
rows.source: People > Will Come row 7 + Won't Come row 1

rows.flag: Ma'am's row is the question itself: "Restricted person should be able to book meeting room yes/no??" Unanswered. Note this is about what the person can DO, not who can see them — the only row in the list of that kind.

portals.name: Payroll
portals.note: The person is paid here, so they are never removed. Payroll shows them to whoever can already open payroll.

rows.treatment: Highlighted row + "Includes N hidden profiles" on the count
rows.flag: MY CALL: ma'am wrote "Highlight Restricted row" only on Employees Compensation and Tax Declaration. Rows 3-6 name the screen with no treatment. Applying the same highlight to all six is consistent, but it is my inference, not her instruction.

rows.treatment: Highlighted row (see the note on Salary Register)
Highlighted row (see the note on Salary Register)
Highlighted row (see the note on Salary Register)

portals.name: Recruitment
portals.note: Nothing in this portal shows a hidden profile. Both rows are exclusions.

rows.treatment: Absent from the selectable panellist list
rows.flag: This is an ELIGIBILITY rule, not only a visibility one: the person cannot be chosen as a panellist. If an existing panellist is later marked hidden, what happens to interviews already scheduled with them is NOT CAPTURED.

rows.treatment: Name not shown to the external viewer

portals.name: CRM & Invoice
portals.note: Here the rule is about the RECORDS the person created, not about the person's row.

rows.flag: Ma'am's row reads "if the person is/has the restricted employee under the team/organization" and stops. It sits under Will Come, so the person appears — but it never says to whom. Cannot be built from this.

rows.screen: Contacts, Companies, Leads, Deals, Client Interviews, Invoices, Payments
rows.treatment: Records created by the person are filtered out
rows.flag: This filters RECORDS BY THEIR CREATOR, not employee rows. It is a different mechanism from every other row in this brief and touches seven record types. Largest engineering item in the list.

portals.name: Project Management
portals.note: Entirely undecided. Ma'am wrote this portal as questions, not rules.

rows.flag: Ma'am's decision tree, unanswered: (1) Should the person be allowed into a project as a resource? (2) If YES — should the tickets assigned to them be visible to everyone? (3) If NO — they cannot be added as a resource at all. Answer (1) first; it decides whether (2) exists.

Ma'am wrote "only the reporting manager will decide the same" — decide, not see. That may mean the RM controls the allocation rather than that the RM is the only viewer. Read here as RM-only visibility; confirm.
